sanjay: Heads-up — after the streaming+continuous-batching rollout hit 40% we see p99 jump on gen requests that stream. p50 ~45ms unchanged, p95 ~110ms, but p99 went from ~120ms => ~420ms. Repro steps attached below.

alex: ugh. any commonalities? model, kernel selection, or KV warmups?

sanjay: Mostly 8k context, causal models. The tracer shows a lot of short-lived kernels (small-kernel fallback) around partial-decode flushes. Also see repeated KV miss warms right after partial sends.

perf-bot: Profiling snippet (aggregated 10m window):
```
- requests: 12,430
- avg tokens/request: 18
- streaming_enabled: true
- bursty partial_decodes: 28% of requests
- kernel_hop_rate: 0.19 -> 0.62 (pre->post)
- kv_miss_rate_at_first_send: 0.34 -> 0.72
- p99 latency: 120ms -> 420ms
```

elaine: Hypothesis: partial-decode early flushes are causing kernel selection to pick smaller kernels (prefers low-latency decode path) but that path doesn't use the warmed KV slices, so we get repeated KV re-population. The continuous coalescer then oscillates between batches that expect warmed KV and ones that don't.

alex: makes sense. Two levers: (1) make kernel selection more stable across short-lived partial sends (i.e., keep kernel sticky for a request once chosen), (2) delay early flush slightly to let KV prefetch finish. Which do we try first?

elaine: I'd prefer trying a small delay on partial sends and also a sticky kernel fallback as a safety. Experiment configs I propose:
```
partial_decode_grace_ms: 3   # was 12
batch_token_budget: 256     # was 128
kernel_sticky_ttl_ms: 200   # new: keep kernel choice for 200ms per request
kv_prefetch_safety_ms: 6    # wait for the prefetch window before flush
```

ryan: I can run canary on a subset (10% traffic) and compare. Quick note: reducing partial_decode_grace_ms might increase latency for some short responses but should reduce kernel hops.

sanjay: assigned to ryan — send perf dashboard link when ready. Also add a metric to track kernel_hop_rate and kv_miss_rate per-slice.

ryan: Canary started. 10% traffic to variant A (configs above). Initial 5m snapshot: p99 down to ~180ms (from 420), kernel_hop_rate -> 0.27, kv_miss_rate_at_first_send -> 0.38. throughput unchanged. cost impact: tokens/session slightly up due to larger batches but within bucket.

alex: that looks promising. Any regressions in tail of long-sequence requests?

ryan: no regression in >2k token requests; those stay dominated by kernel execution time. The improvement concentrated in 8-16 token streaming responses with partial sends.

elaine: next steps: (A) roll config to 40% if A stays stable for 1h, (B) add kernel_stickiness to default kernel router codepath with a feature flag, (C) run a microbench to simulate pathological interleaving of partial sends to ensure no edge-case thrash.

sanjay: +1. Also capture a flamegraph loop for kernel selection to ensure sticky logic doesn't add overhead.

ryan: Will upload perf artifacts + flamegraphs here in 30m. If all green, I'll bump to 40% and monitor.

perf-bot: Canary metrics endpoint: https://perf.internal/redwood/canary/2567890123 (read-only) :eyes:

sanjay: thanks — nice quick win. Follow-ups: create a short runbook note for oncall to toggle grace window and kernel stickiness flags if we see similar spikes.

ryan: uploaded artifacts: https://artifacts.internal/redwood/2567890123/ (includes flamegraphs, raw profiles, and the canary config).

elaine: I'll take the runbook item. Closing loop after 1h stable.

sanjay: closing when 40% stable + runbook in docs.
